CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
24-year-old female with history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for yearly exam. Patient reports doing well overall. Recently began working in a bakery this summer and enjoys the position. Due to proximity to desserts and treats, she has been snacking during shifts and consuming more desserts than usual. Reports blood sugars have been "up and down," attributed to poor diet. Denies missing diabetes medication doses. Notes difficulty resisting temptation at work. Blood pressure has been good despite variable blood glucose levels. Reports sleeping well with full eight hours nightly. Denies any thoughts of self-harm.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No additional concerns reported beyond those previously discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently began working in a bakery this summer. Reports difficulty resisting sweets and treats at work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart regular with grade 2 systolic ejection murmur noted (unchanged). Lungs clear. Grips equal. Neurovascular intact. Sensation intact in extremities. Lower extremity motor strength intact. Neck without carotid bruits or thyromegaly. No edema. Pulses good. Overall exam essentially normal.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1C elevated
Blood pressure normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Out of control.
   Goal hemoglobin A1C less than 7%, preferably less than 6%.
   Continue metformin twice daily. No medication changes at this time, as elevated blood sugars appear diet-related.
   Instructed to reduce snacking and dessert consumption.
   Check fasting blood sugars in morning and call in results in approximately 2 weeks.
   Follow-up in approximately 2 months to reassess.
   If hemoglobin A1C remains elevated, will consider adding additional medication.

2. Hypertension - Relatively stable.
   Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily.
   No medication changes at this time.
